header: THE SECOND TAB OF THE RAILWAY CARD: ASANSOL RAILWAY JUNCTION (ASN), the trains a person at Durgapur can only have by going to Asansol. I show two lists side by side, as the Durgapur tab has its two directions:
* trains that pass Durgapur WITHOUT stopping and stop at Asansol (take them from Asansol);
* trains that do not go over Durgapur at all and stop at Asansol.

A train that stops at Durgapur too is not here (it can be had at Durgapur). The local (MEMU) trains of Asansol are below, in violet, as on the Durgapur tab. Each train shows its time AT ASANSOL (the departure large, the arrival under it), its name and number, where it starts and ends, and the days it is at Asansol, and the saved FARES FROM ASANSOL (₹ Fares: to the end of its run, and to every stop after Asansol), as at Durgapur. It is the timetable, not live running status; the data and its checks are in src/lib/live/railwayAsansol.ts. I ask for the tab's data only when the tab is opened (src/tools/railway/RailwayTabs.tsx mounts this panel then). Nothing typed is sent anywhere.

behaviours: the tab names the station and its code, says how many trains are here and why (they do not stop at Durgapur), and how many are of each kind
it explains that the times and days are those AT ASANSOL, and that 'here' means Asansol
two lists side by side: 'Pass Durgapur without stopping' (5) and 'Do not go over Durgapur' (5 express and special), then the violet MEMU section (1)
each train says which kind it is: a rose chip 'Passes Durgapur, no stop' (5) or a grey 'Not via Durgapur' (6), each with a hover note
a train shows its time at Asansol (the Rajdhani 12302: 07:20, arr 07:18), name, number and class, its two ends with the codes, and the days at Asansol
a train that starts at Asansol says 'starts here', one that ends there 'ends here'

each train that goes on from Asansol has a ₹ Fares button (the MEMU a ₹ Fare hint); a train that ends at Asansol (03512, 12941) has none, there is no fare box until it is pressed, and the intro says the fares are from Asansol
the special train is marked Special; with specials off it is gone; with 'only today' on, a train of other days is gone (12937 runs on Monday only)
the switches are buttons that say whether they are on
the next train that runs today is marked, in its own list, with the wait

the Asansol tab has the same features as the Durgapur tab: the legend (amber junction, premium badges, violet MEMU), the fare finder (going from Asansol), the two switches, the short forms (the Vande Bharat and Shatabdi badges come with the same row code, tested on the Durgapur tab)

the tab says plainly it is the timetable, NOT live running status, how the two kinds are told apart (Durgapur's timetable lists the trains that go through without stopping), and links NTES and RailRadar in new tabs
the short forms are written out at the bottom, as on the Durgapur tab
the railway card has two tabs, named in full: 'Durgapur Railway Station (DGR)' selected first and 'Asansol Railway Junction (ASN)'
the Asansol tab is not asked for until it is opened: its panel is hidden and empty, the Durgapur panel is shown
starting on the Asansol tab shows it first (loading), asks for the Asansol route only, and hides the Durgapur panel
the panel's title names both stations and its subtitle says what is in it, without repeating the title (the tabs below carry the full station names), and its card is the two-tab card
the fare boxes of the Asansol tab ask the routes with from=ASN, and the routes accept only ASN (anything else means Durgapur), reading Asansol's own tables
the Asansol tab's fares say Asansol, not Durgapur: the table heading, the day asked, the km column and the stops text

the fare finder of the Asansol tab asks with from=ASN, and its route accepts only ASN (anything else means Durgapur), keeps each station's list apart, reads Asansol's own leg tables and Asansol's timetable

both timetable routes keep their last good answer in the database and show it, marked stale with its own time, when RailRadar does not answer; Asansol's list is kept three days (two requests each time)
a saved copy is shown only when it is the shape the card draws: the parsed lists pass, anything else does not
the route reads nothing of the caller, and the two addresses asked are fixed in the code (Asansol's board, and Durgapur's with the pass-throughs)
